newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says oil reserves at 9.0 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says oil reserves at 9.0 bln in 1996.

text.p: Algeria's proven crude oil reserves stood at nine billion tonnes at the end of 1996 and its natural gas reserves were at 5.1 trillion cubic metres, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.

APS quoted Energy and Mining Minister Amar Makhloufi as saying the oil recovery rate, currently at about 28 percent, could reach between 35 and 40 percent by the year 2000 if new technologies were introduced and the necessary finances found.
Oil and gas are Algeria's economic mainstay. The value of the North African country's oil and gas exports rose 29 percent in 1996 to $12.6 billion, according to official figures.

The increase was mainly due to higher international oil prices, giving Algeria's crude oil an average of $21.6 per barrel in 1996 against a government budgeted average of $16-$17 per barrel for that year.
